recommendations.headline: Satisfaction is the single biggest lever on conversion: satisfied calls close at 72% vs 15% for neutral and 6% for dissatisfied calls, yet only 33% of calls (656/1974) are rated satisfied and reps leave 68% of calls (1343) without even discussing price.
behaviour: 907 of 1974 calls (46%) end in callback vs only 391 (20%) in an order - customers delay decisions and need structured follow-up.
335 customers behave as price_shoppers and 203 are comparing_quotes, often referencing JSW (52), Tata (36) and Asian (21) as benchmarks.
Price is discussed in only 32% of calls (631/1974) while 'price_high' is still the top objection (285 calls, 14%), showing reps often skip pricing instead of handling it.
Top customer needs are fast_delivery (361), stock_availability (330) and technical_advice (318), yet rep_missed data shows 321 calls had slow/unclear answers and 82 didn't even ask requirement.
201 calls show urgent_buyer behaviour and 264 calls are high urgency, but no_follow_up_fixed (298) and no_quote_sent (179) suggest urgency is not being matched with speed.
satisfaction: Only 656 of 1974 calls (33%) are rated satisfied; 1030 (52%) are neutral and 162 (8%) dissatisfied - most calls are not actively delighting customers.
Win rate by satisfaction is stark: satisfied 72%, neutral 15%, dissatisfied 6% - satisfaction swings outcome far more than any other factor.

Price reactions show 68% of calls (1343) never reach a price discussion, only 10% (203) accept price outright and just 3% (61) call it too high - price is less of a blocker than call execution (price_blocker_pct is only 17%).
Price_high is the most-cited objection (285 calls) but still converts at 27% - comparable to delivery_time (27%) and quality_doubt (28%), showing price alone rarely kills a deal when handled well.

conversion.title: Fix call execution quality first
conversion.evidence: 321 calls flagged slow_or_unclear_answer; satisfied calls convert at 72% vs 15% neutral/6% dissatisfied
conversion.action: Coach reps on clear, confident, quick responses; managers to spot-check calls weekly against a clarity checklist.

conversion.title: Always quote price before ending the call
conversion.evidence: 1343 calls (68%) never discuss price; 179 calls had no_quote_sent
conversion.action: Make it mandatory to share at least an indicative rate or WhatsApp quote on every enquiry call before hang-up.

conversion.title: Always ask for the order
conversion.action: Train reps to explicitly close with 'Shall I confirm this order?' once interest or price acceptance is shown.

conversion.title: Put every callback on a fixed schedule
conversion.evidence: 907 calls (46%) end in callback; 298 calls had no_follow_up_fixed
conversion.action: Require reps to log a specific date/time for next contact in CRM and set auto-reminders; manager audits weekly.

conversion.title: Offer alternatives when stock is short
conversion.evidence: stock_availability is the 2nd top objection (262 calls, 25% win); 104 calls show didnt_offer_alternative
conversion.action: Build a quick-reference alternate-stock/colour list so reps can offer substitutes instead of saying 'no stock'.

conversion.title: Strengthen technical readiness on calls
conversion.evidence: 282 calls show needs_technical_help and technical_advice is the 3rd top need (318 calls)
conversion.action: Equip reps with a technical cheat-sheet (thickness, gauge, length limits) and escalate complex specs to a technical point person in real time.

conversion.title: Prioritise and re-qualify 'unknown' segment leads
conversion.evidence: Unknown segment has 694 calls but only 25% win rate vs dealer 40% and builder 40%
conversion.action: Add a mandatory segment-tagging question early in the call to route unknown leads to the right pitch and pricing track.

offers.title: Tiered bulk/dealer pricing plan
offers.why: Bulk and dealer segments already show highest win rates; formalising tiers can speed up negotiation calls (314 are currently 'negotiating').

offers.title: Cutting & customisation service package
offers.for_whom: Customers needing cutting_processing (83) and custom lengths
offers.why: Multiple calls request custom cutting/length (e.g. 7.2m, 20ft, puff sheets) that reps currently decline or delay.

offers.title: Sample/swatch and colour-match service
offers.for_whom: Customers needing samples (52) and colour consistency (off-white, sky blue mismatches noted)
offers.why: Several well-converted calls involved sending photos/samples via WhatsApp before order confirmation.

offers.title: Priority/same-day dispatch service
offers.why: fast_delivery is the top customer need (361) and several urgent requests (same-night, 1.5-hour delivery) were only partially met.

offers.title: Stock-alert/waitlist system
offers.why: stock_availability is the top need (330) and 2nd top objection (262); proactive alerts could convert delayed enquiries.

offers.title: Evaluate structured credit terms for regular dealers
offers.for_whom: needs_credit customers (65) and credit_terms objection (57, 26% win)
offers.why: Credit-related asks recur in both objections and needs; a clear policy could reduce stalled negotiations.

loyalty.title: Formal referral recognition programme
loyalty.how: Track referral-sourced leads (21 flagged) and acknowledge/reward the referring customer with priority service or account perks
loyalty.why: Referral behaviour already appears organically in calls (e.g. 'referred by an engineer') and customers ask about referral benefits.

loyalty.title: Repeat-buyer priority desk
loyalty.how: Flag repeat_buyers (178) and loyal_to_us (17) in CRM for faster call handling and a known point of contact
loyalty.why: Repeat buyers already show consistent ordering patterns (e.g. 'usual 2.5m length') - recognising this builds stickiness.

loyalty.title: Consider tiered credit period for proven dealers
loyalty.how: Offer extended credit days to dealers with a clean payment history, reviewed quarterly
loyalty.why: credit_period is a named need (58) and credit_terms objection has decent win rate (26%) when resolved.

loyalty.title: Proactive status-update commitment
loyalty.how: Set fixed intervals (e.g. every 2 days) to update customers on production/delivery status without being asked
loyalty.why: regular_updates is a top need (157) and no_follow_up_fixed (298) is a major rep gap.

loyalty.title: Dedicated account manager for top-volume dealers
loyalty.how: Assign single point of contact for high-frequency dealer accounts (969 dealer calls)
loyalty.why: Dealers already have the highest win rate (40%); a dedicated manager can protect and grow this base.

loyalty.title: Quality documentation on demand
loyalty.how: Proactively offer test certificates/warranty details with every quote, not just on request
loyalty.why: test_certificate need (15) and quality_doubt objection (79, 28% win) show trust-building potential.

non_price_benefits.title: Technical expertise on every call
non_price_benefits.why: technical_advice is the 3rd highest need (318) and needs_technical_help behaviour appears in 282 calls.

non_price_benefits.title: Reliable, transparent stock status
non_price_benefits.why: stock_availability is the top customer need (330) and 2nd top objection (262).

non_price_benefits.title: Fast and committed delivery timelines
non_price_benefits.why: fast_delivery is the single largest need (361), and many stalled calls cite vague delivery promises.

non_price_benefits.title: Quality assurance and certification support
non_price_benefits.why: quality_assurance need (100) plus quality_doubt objection converts well (28%) when properly addressed.

non_price_benefits.title: Customisation and cutting capability
non_price_benefits.why: cutting_processing need (83) and frequent custom-length/size requests in call summaries.

non_price_benefits.title: Consistency of supply for repeat orders
non_price_benefits.why: consistent_supply need (98) and repeat_buyer behaviour (178) show customers value dependable restocking.

top_questions.question: What is the current rate for [product/thickness/colour]?
top_questions.answer_tip: Always give a clear current rate or quote reference and note validity period, without needing manager escalation.

top_questions.question: Is [specific colour/thickness] in stock right now?
top_questions.answer_tip: Check live stock on the call; if unavailable, immediately offer the closest alternative colour/thickness.

top_questions.question: What is the delivery time/can you deliver today?
top_questions.answer_tip: Give a specific committed date/time based on dispatch schedule rather than an open-ended 'we'll check'.

top_questions.question: Can you cut/customise the sheet to my required length?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm machine capability and lead time clearly; if not possible, explain the nearest available option.

top_questions.question: Can you provide credit terms or extended payment?
top_questions.answer_tip: Explain the credit evaluation process and documentation needed, and set expectation on response time.

top_questions.question: Why did the price change after I submitted the PO?
top_questions.answer_tip: Explain price validity windows clearly at quote stage and escalate immediately if a dispute arises, rather than letting it go unresolved.

top_questions.question: Does the product carry warranty/test certification?
top_questions.answer_tip: Proactively share warranty terms and offer to send test certificates along with the quote.

top_questions.question: What discount is available for bulk/carton orders?
top_questions.answer_tip: Reference the applicable volume-based scheme and next steps to confirm quantity, without stating specific figures on the call.
